messages:
sam.sales: Hey team — POC kickoff with FinVault tomorrow. They want a Dedicated endpoint but can only allow a small set of customer egress IPs on their firewall. Can we confirm options for: static egress IPs per pool, short-lived rotation, or a proxy approach? Also they asked about any extra fees for static IPs and timeline for provisioning.

julia.solutions: short answer: we can do a few approaches. longer: Dedicated pools can be fronted by a NAT with static IP(s) per customer for Dedicated (extra config + optional charge). For POC we usually do a temporary allowlist + proxy.

kevin.eng: details — we have three workable patterns: 1) Static egress IP assigned to the Dedicated pool (preferred for prod). 2) Customer sets up reverse proxy tunnel to our ingress (works for air-gapped-ish setups). 3) Private/VPC peering for full isolation (requires customer infra).

kevin.eng: For POC I'd recommend: create a temporary NAT with 2 static IPs, provide those to the customer for allowlisting, then switch to the long-term plan. Provisioning time ~24–48h if infra slot is free.

louise.sre: note on rotation: if customer insists on IP rotation, we can support rotation windows but they need to allow the full CIDR or automate allowlist updates on their side. We don't rotate the static IPs automatically without coordination. :warning:

sam.sales: @julia.solutions @kevin.eng perfect. They are also asking about host auth — they prefer mTLS to the endpoint. Is that supported on Dedicated endpoints?

julia.solutions: We support TLS by default. mTLS is available on Private deployments and can be added to Dedicated with an enterprise config (needs certs and a small infra change). For POC we can enable a simple client-cert check on the edge, but that adds setup time (~2 business days).

kevin.eng: + pricing note: static egress IP per pool = one-time setup fee + small monthly IP surcharge. For POC we can waive the setup fee if the customer commits to a paid POC (sales-led). I'll defer exact numbers to sales ops.

sam.sales: Can we give them a test curl they can run once we hand over the static IPs so they can validate firewall rules?

kevin.eng: yes — provide them with an origin IP test and a short curl to exercise token auth. Example we give them (put these behind their firewall):

```
# from customer's bastion, verify egress IP
curl -s https://ifconfig.co

# call endpoint (replace IP with our NAT IP)
curl -X POST https://dedicated-rw.example.net/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

louise.sre: small ops checklist for POC: 1) create Dedicated pool + NAT config 2) reserve 2 static IPs 3) generate POC API key and limited quotas 4) enable TLS (and mTLS if requested) 5) share IPs + curl + expiry window with customer 6) monitor logs for blocked connections.

sam.sales: timeline for us to hand IPs to the customer?

kevin.eng: if we start today and infra queue is clear: create pool + NAT = same-day for staging, 24–48h for production-grade NAT + certs. If they want mTLS add ~48h.

julia.solutions: I've asked sales-ops for fee waiver for POC (cc @alex). I'll update thread when I hear back.

infra-bot: Ticket INF-2026 created for Dedicated POC provisioning (owner: kevin.eng). ETA: 2026-05-08.

sam.sales: Great — i'll tell FinVault we can supply 2 static egress IPs for allowlisting, can do mTLS with a couple days extra, and provide a curl test. Thanks all :thumbsup:

louise.sre: one last thing — add the customer's expected egress volume to the ticket so we size the pool correctly. If they're running heavy batch requests we may suggest a larger Dedicated pool to meet latency SLOs.

sam.sales: noted, i'll add approximate RPS and token estimates to INF-2026 today.

julia.solutions: awesome. keep me posted and i'll prepare the POC handover doc (IP list, curl, expiry, support contacts).
